label: ex:mech
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:mech}
{\rm  Consider a linear mechanical system with configuration coordinates $q$ subject to geometric constraints $G_\mu^\top {q} = 0$ for some matrix $G_\mu$. The Hamiltonian is of the form kinetic energy plus potential energy:
 
\[
\mathcal{H}_1(q,p)= \frac{1}{2} p^\top M^{-1}p + \frac{1}{2}q^\top \Phi q,
\]
 
where $p=M\dot{q}$ are the momenta, and $\Phi=\Phi^\top$ is a matrix defining the potential energy. Note that the geometric constraints $G_\mu^\top {q} = 0$ are \emph{Lagrange} algebraic constraints, corresponding to the singular Lagrange structure
 
\[
\mathcal{L}= \{(q,p,e_q,e_p) \mid \begin{bmatrix} e_q \\ e_p \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} \Phi & 0 \\ 0 & M^{-1} \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} q \\ p \end{bmatrix} \in \mbox{\rm im\,} \begin{bmatrix} G_\mu \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, G_\mu^\top {q} = 0 \},
\]
 
which can be equivalently written as
 
\[
\mathcal{L}= \{(q,p,e_q,e_p) \mid \exists \ \mu \mbox{ s.t. } \begin{bmatrix} e_q \\ e_p \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \Phi & 0 \\ 0 & M^{-1} \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} q \\ p \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} G_\mu \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \mu, G_\mu^\top {q} = 0 \}.
\]
 
Thus, the regular augmented Lagrange structure $\mathcal{L}_a$ in the augmented state  $x_a=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}q^\top & p^\top & \mu^\top\end{array}\right]^\top$ is given as
 
\[
\mathcal{L}_a= \left \{(q,p,\mu, e_q,e_p, e_\mu) \mid \begin{bmatrix} e_q \\ e_p \\ e_\mu \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \Phi & 0 & G_\mu \\ 0 & M^{-1} & 0 \\ G_\mu^\top & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} q \\ p \\ \mu \end{bmatrix} \right \}.
\]
 
Correspondingly, the singular augmented Dirac structure is
 
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{D}_a = \left \{(f_q,f_p,f_\mu, e_q,e_p,e_\mu)) \mid \begin{bmatrix} I & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} f_q \\ f_p \\ f_\mu \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & I & 0 \\-I & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 &I \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} e_q \\ e_p \\ e_\mu \end{bmatrix} =0 \right \}.
\end{equation*}
 
Taken together, this results in the augmented pHDAE system
 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&
\left[\begin{array}{ccc} I & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]
\left[\begin{array}{cccc} I & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & I \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c} \dot {q} \\ \dot {p} \\ \dot \mu \end{array}\right] \\  && \qquad
=
\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 0 & I & 0 \\ -I & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 0  & I \end{array}\right] \left[\begin{array}{ccc} \Phi & 0 & G_\mu \\ 0 & M^{-1} & 0 \\ G_\mu^\top  & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]
\left[\begin{array}{c}q \\ p \\ \mu \end{array}\right].
\end{eqnarray*}
 
As a consequence, the Lagrange algebraic constraints $G_\mu^\top q=0$ for the original system have been converted into Dirac algebraic constraints for the augmented system.
}

label: ex:mech2
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:mech2}{\rm  Consider the mechanical system  from Example~\ref{ex:mech}, but now subject to \emph{kinematic} constraints $G_\lambda^\top \dot{q} = 0$ for some matrix $G_\lambda$. Inserting $\dot q=M^{-1}p$, the kinematic constraints can be expressed as the Dirac algebraic constraint $G_\lambda^\top M^{-1}p =0$.
  
                                                       
                                                                
                          

By d'Alembert's principle the kinematic constraints give rise to constraint forces $G_\lambda \lambda$ for some vector of Lagrange multipliers $\lambda$. This results in the extended pHDAE of the form \eqref{kpls} in  $x_a=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}q^\top & p^\top & \lambda^\top\end{array}\right]^\top$ given by
 
\begin{eqnarray*}\nonumber
&&
\left[\begin{array}{ccc} I & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & I \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ccc} I & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \left[\begin{array}{c}\dot{q} \\ \dot{p} \\ \dot{\lambda} \end{array}\right] \\
&&  \qquad=
\begin{bmatrix} 0 & I & 0 \\ -I & 0 & G_\lambda \\ 0 & -G_\lambda^\top  & 0 \end{bmatrix} \left[\begin{array}{ccc} \Phi & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & M^{-1} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & I \end{array}\right]
\left[\begin{array}{c}q \\ p \\ \lambda \end{array}\right],
                 
\end{eqnarray*}
 
where again the Hamiltonian is
 
\[
\mathcal{H}_2(q,p,\lambda)= \frac{1}{2} p^\top M^{-1}p + \frac{1}{2}q^\top \Phi q.
\]
 
}

title: Proposition
body_md: Consider a port-Hamiltonian DAE system $(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{L})$ on a state space manifold $\mathcal{X}$, where the Dirac structure $\mathcal{D}$ is \emph{singular}, while the Lagrangian submanifold $\mathcal{L}$ is \emph{regular}. Then it can be augmented to a port-Hamiltonian DAE system $(\mathcal{D}_a,\mathcal{L}_a)$ on the augmented space manifold $\mathcal{X}_a$ with regular Dirac structure and singular Lagrangian submanifold. Furthermore, the $x$-dynamics of this augmented system is the same as of the original system.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: Consider a port-Hamiltonian DAE system $(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{L})$ with Lagrange algebraic constraints. Represent $\mathcal{L}$ by a Morse family $F(x,\mu)$ on $\mathcal{X}_a= \mathcal{X} \times \Lambda$ as in \eqref{morse}, and define the augmented Dirac structure $\mathcal{D}_a$ as the product of $\mathcal{D}$ with the Dirac structure $\{(f_{\mu},e_{\lambda}) \mid e_{\mu}=0 \}$. Then $(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{L})$ has been transformed into the port-Hamiltonian system $(\mathcal{D}_a,\mathcal{L}_a)$ with state space $\mathcal{X}_a$, in such a way that its $x$-dynamics is the same as that of the original port-Hamiltonian DAE system.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite-dimensional linear space. A subspace $\mathcal{M} \subset \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}^*$ is called a \emph{monotone structure} if the quadratic form defined by the bilinear form $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_+$ is nonnegative on $\mathcal{M}$. It is a maximally monotone structure if moreover $\mathcal{M}$ is maximal with respect to this property, i.e., there does not exist another monotone structure $\mathcal{M}'$ with $M \subsetneqq \mathcal{M}'$.

label: prop:maxmon
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:maxmon}
The matrix
 
\[
\mathcal{M} = \operatorname{im} \begin{bmatrix} V \\ W \end{bmatrix}
\]
 
is the image representation of a maximally monotone structure if and only if for every  maximal annihilator $
\left[\begin{array}{cc} F & G\end{array}\right]$ of $\mathcal{M}$ one has $GF^\top+F G^\top \leq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $\mathcal{M}= \ker \begin{bmatrix} F & G \end{bmatrix}$ with $F$ \emph{invertible}, then the $(f,e) \in \mathcal{M}$ are satisfying $f= - F^{-1}Ge$. Since $<e \mid f> \, \geq \, 0$ for all $(f,e) \in \mathcal{M}$, it follows that $e^\top F^{-1}Ge \leq 0$ for all $e$. Thus $F^{-1}G + G^\top F^{-\top} \leq 0$, or equivalently $GF^\top + FG^\top \leq 0$.
On the other hand, if $\mathcal{M}$ is such that $F$ is \emph{not} invertible, then arbitrarily close to $\mathcal{M}$ there will exist a maximally monotone $\mathcal{M}'$ with associated $F'$ being invertible, and thus by continuity $GF^\top + FG^\top \leq 0$ remains to hold.
\space
       {\ \vbox{\hrule\hbox{\vrule height1.3ex\hskip0.8ex\vrule}\hrule}}
       \bigskip

These observations are  immediately extended to linear dissipative port-Hamiltonian systems with \emph{external ports}. In fact, let $\mathcal{F}_P \times \mathcal{E}_P$, with $\mathcal{E}_P=\mathcal{F}_P^*$ (here the index $P$ denotes external ports), be the space of external flows and efforts (inputs and outputs). Then a linear dissipative port-Hamiltonian system with external ports is specified by a maximally monotone structure
$\mathcal{M} \subset \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}^* \times \mathcal{F}_P \times \mathcal{E}_P$,
together with a Lagrange structure $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}^*$ modeling energy storage.

After recalling the extension of linear port-Hamiltonian DAE systems to system with resistive and external ports, in the next subsection we proceed analogously for the nonlinear case.
